verses.39:15: For thus says the Lord: Fields and houses and vineyards will again be established in this land."
verses.39:16: And I prayed to the Lord after I had given the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, saying,
verses.39:17: "O Existing One, Lord, You made heaven and earth by Your great strength and by Your high and uplifted arm; nothing will be hidden from You,
verses.39:18: showing mercy to thousands and repaying the sins of fathers into the bosoms of their children after them, the great God, the mighty One,
verses.39:19: Lord of great counsel and powerful in works, the great God, the Almighty, and Lord of great name; Your eyes are upon the ways of the sons of men, to give to each according to his way;
verses.39:20: You who performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt until this day, both in Israel and among the earthborn, and You made for Yourself a name as it is this day,
verses.39:21: and You brought Your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and with wonders, with a strong hand
verses.39:22: and with a high arm and with great visions, and You gave them this land which You swore to their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.39:23: And they went in and took it, and they did not listen to Your voice, and they did not walk in Your ordinances; all that You commanded them they did not do, so that all these evils happened to them.
verses.39:24: Look, a crowd has come to the city to capture it, and the city has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans who are fighting against it, because of the sword and the famine; just as You spoke, so it has happened.
verses.39:25: And You say to me, 'Buy for yourself the field for silver.' And I wrote a deed and sealed it, and called witnesses, and the city has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans."
verses.39:26: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.39:27: "I am the Lord, the God of all flesh; will anything be hidden from Me?
verses.39:28: Therefore thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: This city will surely be handed over into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he will take it,
verses.39:29: and the Chaldeans will come fighting against this city, and they will burn this city with fire, and burn down the houses in which they burned incense on their rooftops to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods in order to provoke Me to bitterness.
verses.39:30: For the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah alone have been doing what is evil before My eyes from their youth;
verses.39:31: for this city has been for My anger and for My wrath, from the day they built it even until this day, to remove it from My presence,
verses.39:32: because of all the wicked acts of the sons of Israel and of Judah which they did to embitter Me, they and their kings and their rulers and their priests and their prophets, the men of Judah and those who dwell in Jerusalem.
verses.39:33: And they turned their back to Me and not their face, and I taught them early in the morning and taught them, yet they no longer listened to receive discipline.
verses.39:34: And they placed their defilements in the house upon which My name was called, in their impurities.
verses.39:35: And they built the altars to Baal that are in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to offer up their sons and their daughters to Molech the king, things which I did not command them and which did not come up into My heart, that they should do this abomination, so that Judah would sin.
verses.39:36: And now thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning the city of which you say, 'It will be handed over into the hands of the king of Babylon by sword and by famine and by banishment':
verses.39:37: Look, I am gathering them from all the earth where I scattered them in My anger and My wrath and great indignation, and I will bring them back to this place, and I will settle them in confidence,
verses.39:38: and they will be a people to Me, and I will be God to them.
verses.39:39: And I will give them another way and another heart, to fear Me all the days, and for good to them and to their children after them.
verses.39:40: And I will make an eternal covenant with them, which I will by no means turn away from behind them; and I will put My fear into their heart, so that they will not depart from Me.
verses.39:41: And I will visit them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land in faithfulness and with all heart and with all soul.
verses.39:42: For thus says the Lord: Just as I brought upon this people all these great evils, so I will bring upon them all the good things that I have spoken concerning them.
verses.39:43: And fields will again be bought in the land of which you say, 'It will be impassable, without people and livestock, and they have been handed over into the hands of the Chaldeans.'
verses.39:44: And they will buy fields with silver, and you will write a deed and seal it, and call witnesses, in the land of Benjamin, and around Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, and in the cities of the hill country of the Shephelah, and in the cities of the Negev; for I will restore their exiles."
verses.40:1: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still bound in the court of the guard, saying,
verses.40:2: "Thus says the Lord, who makes the earth and forms it to establish it, the Lord is His name:
verses.40:3: Call out to Me and I will answer you, and I will declare to you great and mighty things that you did not know.
verses.40:4: For thus says the Lord concerning the houses of this city and concerning the houses of the king of Judah that have been torn down for ramparts and bulwarks,
verses.40:5: to fight against the Chaldeans and to fill it with the dead bodies of the people whom I struck down in My anger and in My wrath, and I turned My face away from them because of all their wicked acts:
verses.40:6: Look, I am bringing up for it recovery and healing, and I will reveal to them, and I will heal it, both peace and faithfulness;
verses.40:7: and I will restore the exiles of Judah and the exiles of Israel, and I will build them up just as before,
verses.40:8: and I will cleanse them from all their iniquities by which they sinned against Me, and I will by no means remember their sins by which they sinned against Me and departed from Me.
verses.40:9: And it will be for gladness and praise and for majesty to all the people of the earth, who will hear of all the good things that I will do; and they will fear and be embittered because of all the good things and because of all the peace that I will make for them.
verses.40:10: Thus says the Lord: Again there will be heard in this place of which you say, 'It is desolate, without people and livestock,' in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem, which have been made desolate because there is no person and no livestock,
verses.40:11: the voice of gladness and the voice of joy, the voice of a bridegroom and the voice of a bride, the voice of those saying, 'Give thanks to the Lord Almighty, for the Lord is good, for His mercy is forever,' and they will bring gifts into the house of the Lord; for I will restore all the exiles of that land as before, says the Lord.
verses.40:12: Thus says the Lord of powers: In this place, which is desolate because there is no person and no livestock, in all its cities there will be resting places of shepherds making sheep lie down;
verses.40:13: in the cities of the hill country, and in the cities of the Shephelah, and in the cities of the Negev, and in the land of Benjamin, and in those around Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, sheep will again pass by the hand of one who counts, says the Lord."
verses.41:1: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord—and Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army and all the land of his dominion were fighting against him, against Jerusalem and against all the cities of Judah—saying,
verses.41:2: "Thus said the Lord: Go to Zedekiah king of Judah, and you shall say to him, 'Thus said the Lord: This city will surely be handed over into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it and burn it with fire,
verses.41:3: and you will by no means escape from his hand, and you will surely be captured and be given into his hands, and your eyes will see his eyes, and you will enter Babylon.
verses.41:4: Yet hear the word of the Lord, Zedekiah king of Judah. Thus says the Lord:
verses.41:5: You will die in peace; and just as they wept for your fathers who reigned before you, they will weep for you also, and even to Hades they will mourn for you; for I have spoken a word, said the Lord.'"
verses.41:6: And Jeremiah spoke all these words to King Zedekiah in Jerusalem.
verses.41:7: And the force of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against the cities of Judah, and against Lachish and against Azekah, for these were left among the cities of Judah as fortified cities.
verses.41:8: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after King Zedekiah concluded a covenant with the people to proclaim a release,
verses.41:9: that each one should send away his male servant and each one his female servant, the Hebrew man and the Hebrew woman, free, so that no man from Judah should serve as a slave.
verses.41:10: And all the nobles and all the people who had entered into the covenant that each one should send away his male servant and his female servant turned back, and they left
verses.41:11: them as male servants and female servants.
verses.41:12: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying,
verses.41:13: "Thus said the Lord: I established a covenant with your fathers on the day when I delivered them from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery, saying,
verses.41:14: 'When six years are completed, you shall send away your brother, the Hebrew, who will be sold to you and will work for you six years, and you shall send him away free.' And they did not listen to Me, and they did not incline their ear.
verses.41:15: And they turned back today to do what is right before My eyes, for each one to proclaim a release of his neighbor, and they concluded a covenant before Me in the house upon which My name was called.
verses.41:16: And you turned back and profaned My name by bringing back each one his male servant and each one his female servant, whom you had sent away free to their own will, to be male servants and female servants for you."
verses.41:17: Therefore thus said the Lord: "You did not listen to Me to proclaim a release, each one to his neighbor; look, I am proclaiming a release for you to the sword and to death and to famine, and I will give you over to dispersion among all the kingdoms of the earth.
verses.41:18: And I will give over the men who have transgressed My covenant, who did not uphold My covenant that they made before Me, the calf that they made to serve it,
verses.41:19: the rulers of Judah and the officials and the priests and the people,
verses.41:20: and I will give them to their enemies, and their corpses will be food for the birds of heaven and for the wild beasts of the earth.
verses.41:21: And I will give Zedekiah king of Judea and their rulers into the hands of their enemies, and the force of the king of Babylon is for those who are running away from them.
verses.41:22: Look, I am giving a command," says the Lord, "and I will bring them back to this land, and they will fight against it and take it and burn it down with fire, and the cities of Judah, and I will make them desolate, without inhabitants."
verses.42:1: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim king of Judah, saying,
verses.42:2: "Go to the house of Archabin, and you shall bring them into the house of the Lord, into one of the courts, and you shall give them wine to drink."
verses.42:3: And I brought out Jeconiah son of Jeremin, son of Chabasin, and his brothers and his sons, and all the household of Archabin,
verses.42:4: and I brought them into the house of the Lord, into the chamber of the sons of Jonan son of Hananiah, son of Gedaliah, the man of God, which is near the house of the rulers who are above the house of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the keeper of the court.
verses.42:5: And I set before them a jar of wine and cups, and I said, "Drink wine."
verses.42:6: And they said, "We will by no means drink wine, for Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying, 'You shall by no means drink wine, you and your sons, forever;
verses.42:7: and you shall by no means build a house, and you shall by no means sow seed, and you shall have no vineyard; for you shall dwell in tents all your days, so that you may live many days upon the land where you reside.'
verses.42:8: And we listened to the voice of Jonadab our father, not to drink wine all our days, we and our wives and our sons and our daughters,
verses.42:9: and not to build houses to dwell there; we have had neither vineyard nor field nor seed;
verses.42:10: and we dwelt in tents, and we listened and did according to all that Jonadab our father commanded us.
verses.42:11: And it happened, when Nebuchadnezzar came up against the land, that we said to go in, and we went into Jerusalem from before the force of the Chaldeans and from before the force of the Assyrians; and we were dwelling there."
verses.42:12: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.42:13: "Thus says the Lord: Go and say to the man of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, 'Will you never receive discipline to listen to My words?
verses.42:14: The sons of Jonadab son of Rechab upheld the word that he commanded his children, not to drink wine, and they did not drink; and I spoke to you early in the morning, and I spoke, and you did not listen.
verses.42:15: And I sent to you My servants the prophets, saying, "Turn away, each one from his evil way, and make your practices better, and do not go after other gods to serve them, and you will dwell upon the land that I gave to you and to your fathers." And you did not incline your ears, and you did not listen.
verses.42:16: And the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab upheld the command of their father, but this people did not listen to Me.'"
verses.42:17: Therefore thus said the Lord: "Look, I am bringing upon Judah and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the evils that I spoke against them."
verses.42:18: Therefore thus said the Lord: "Because the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab listened to the command of their father, to do just as their father commanded them,
verses.42:19: there will by no means be lacking a man from the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab standing before Me all the days of the earth."
verses.43:1: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.43:2: "Take for yourself a scroll of a book, and write on it all the words that I have spoken to you against Jerusalem and against Judah and against all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah king of Judah and until this day.
verses.43:3: Perhaps the house of Judah will hear all the evils that I am planning to do to them, so that they may turn back from their evil way, and I will be merciful to their wrongdoings and to their sins."
verses.43:4: And Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and he wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the Lord, which He spoke to him, onto a scroll of a book.
verses.43:5: And Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, "I am kept under guard; I certainly cannot enter the house of the Lord.
verses.43:6: And you shall read from this scroll in the ears of the people in the house of the Lord on a day of fasting, and in the ears of all Judah who come from their city you shall read to them.
verses.43:7: Perhaps their mercy will fall before the Lord, and they will turn back from their evil way, for great is the wrath and the anger of the Lord, which He spoke against this people."
verses.43:8: And Baruch did according to all that Jeremiah commanded him, to read from the book the words of the Lord in the house of the Lord.
verses.43:9: And it happened in the eighth year of King Jehoiakim, in the ninth month, that all the people in Jerusalem and the house of Judah convened a fast before the Lord.
verses.43:10: And Baruch was reading from the book the words of Jeremiah in the house of the Lord, in the house of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court, at the entrance of the new gate of the house of the Lord, and in the ears of all the people.
verses.43:11: And Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the words of the Lord from the book.
verses.43:12: And he went down to the king's house, to the house of the scribe, and look, all the officials were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, and Delaiah son of Shelemiah, and Jonathan son of Achbor, and Gemariah son of Shaphan, and Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the officials.
verses.43:13: And Micaiah declared to them all the words that he heard while Baruch was reading in the ears of the people.
verses.43:14: And all the officials sent to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi, saying, "The scroll from which you are reading in the ears of the people, take it in your hand and come." And Baruch took the scroll and went down to them.
verses.43:15: And they said to him, "Read again in our ears." And Baruch read.
verses.43:16: And it happened, when they heard all the words, that they took counsel, each one with his neighbor, and said, "Let us surely declare to the king all these words."
verses.43:17: And they asked Baruch, saying, "Where did you write all these words?"
verses.43:18: And Baruch said, "From his mouth Jeremiah declared to me all these words, and I was writing in a book."
verses.43:19: And they said to Baruch, "Go, hide yourself, you and Jeremiah; let no one know where you are."
verses.43:20: And they went in to the king into the court, and they gave the scroll to be kept in the house of Elisha, and they declared to the king all the words.
verses.43:21: And the king sent Jehudi to take the scroll. And he took it from the house of Elisha, and Jehudi read in the ears of the king and in the ears of all the officials who were standing around the king.
verses.43:22: And the king was sitting in the winter house, and a brazier of fire was before him.
verses.43:23: And it happened, as Jehudi was reading three and four columns, that he would cut them off with the scribe's razor and throw them into the fire that was on the brazier, until the entire scroll vanished into the fire that was on the brazier.
verses.43:24: And they did not inquire, and they did not tear their garments, the king and his servants who heard all these words.
verses.43:25: And Elnathan and Gedaliah advised the king to burn the scroll.
verses.43:26: And the king commanded Jerahmeel son of the king and Seraiah son of Azriel to seize Baruch and Jeremiah; and they hid themselves.
verses.43:27: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, after the king burned the scroll, all the words that Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah, saying,
verses.43:28: "Again, you take another scroll and write all the words that were on the scroll, which King Jehoiakim burned,
verses.43:29: and you shall say, 'Thus says the Lord: You have burned this scroll, saying, "Why have you written on it, saying, 'The king of Babylon will surely come and destroy this land, and man and livestock will vanish from it'?"
verses.43:30: Therefore thus says the Lord against Jehoiakim king of Judah: He shall have no one sitting on the throne of David, and his corpse shall be thrown out in the heat of the day and in the frost of the night.
verses.43:31: And I will punish him and his offspring and his servants, and I will bring upon him and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem and upon the land of Judah all the evils that I spoke to them, and they did not listen.'"
verses.43:32: And Baruch took another scroll and wrote on it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book that Jehoiakim had burned; and still more words like these were added to it.
verses.44:1: And Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned instead of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar made king to reign over Judah.
verses.44:2: And he and his servants and the people of the land did not listen to the words of the Lord that He spoke by the hand of Jeremiah.
verses.44:3: And King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, the priest, to Jeremiah, saying, "Please pray for us to the Lord."
verses.44:4: And Jeremiah came and passed through the midst of the city, and they had not put him into the prison house.
verses.44:5: And the army of Pharaoh came out of Egypt, and the Chaldeans heard the report of them, and they went up against Jerusalem.
verses.44:6: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying,
verses.44:7: "Thus says the Lord: Thus you shall say to the king of Judah who sent to you to seek Me: 'Look, the army of Pharaoh that came out to help you will return to the land of Egypt,
verses.44:8: and the Chaldeans themselves will come back and fight against this city, and they will capture it and burn it with fire.
verses.44:9: For thus says the Lord: Do not suppose in your souls, saying, "The Chaldeans will surely depart from us," for they will certainly not depart.
verses.44:10: And even if you strike down the entire army of the Chaldeans who are fighting against you, and some who have been pierced through are left behind, each one in his place, these will rise up and burn this city with fire.'"
verses.44:11: And it happened, when the army of the Chaldeans went up from Jerusalem from before the army of Pharaoh,
verses.44:12: that Jeremiah went out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to buy from there in the midst of the people.
verses.44:13: And he was at the Gate of Benjamin, and there was a man with whom he was lodging, Saruiah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah, and he seized Jeremiah, saying, "Are you fleeing to the Chaldeans?"
verses.44:14: And he said, "A lie! I am not fleeing to the Chaldeans." And he did not listen to him, and Saruiah seized Jeremiah and brought him in to the officials.
verses.44:15: And the officials became embittered against Jeremiah and struck him, and they sent him to the house of Jonathan the scribe, because they had made it into a prison house.
verses.44:16: And Jeremiah went into the house of the pit and into the chereth, and he remained there many days.
verses.44:17: And Zedekiah sent and called him, and the king secretly asked him, saying, "Is there a word from the Lord?" And he said, "There is; into the hands of the king of Babylon you will be handed over."
verses.44:18: And Jeremiah said to the king, "What wrong have I done to you and to your servants and to this people, that you are putting me into a prison house?
verses.44:19: And where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, 'The king of Babylon will certainly not come against this land'?
verses.44:20: And now, lord king, let my mercy fall before you; and why are you returning me to the house of Jonathan the scribe, and will I not die there?"
verses.44:21: And the king gave orders, and they threw him into the prison house, and they were giving him one loaf of bread a day from outside where they bake, until the loaves ran out from the city; and Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard.
verses.45:1: And Saphanias son of Nathan, and Gedaliah son of Pashhur, and Jehucal son of Shelemiah heard the words that Jeremiah was speaking to the people, saying,
verses.45:2: "Thus says the Lord: 'The one who dwells in this city will die by sword and by famine, and the one who goes out to the Chaldeans will live, and his life will be as a find, and he will live.'
verses.45:3: For thus says the Lord: 'This city will certainly be handed over into the hands of the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.'"
verses.45:4: And they said to the king, "Please let that man be put to death, because he is weakening the hands of the fighting men who remain in the city and the hands of all the people by speaking to them words like these, for this man does not prophesy peace to this people, but only evil."
verses.45:5: And the king said, "Look, he is in your hands," for the king could not prevail against them.
verses.45:6: And they threw him into the cistern of Malchijah the king's son, which was in the court of the guard, and they lowered him into the cistern; and in the cistern there was no water, only mud, and he was in the mud.
verses.45:7: And Ebed-melech the Ethiopian heard, while he was in the house of the king, that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern; and the king was at the Gate of Benjamin.
verses.45:8: And he went out to him, and spoke to the king and said,
verses.45:9: "You have acted wickedly in what you have done, to kill this man because of the famine, for there are no longer loaves of bread in the city."
verses.45:10: And the king commanded Ebed-melech, saying, "Take thirty men from here into your hands, and bring him up out of the cistern so that he may not die."
verses.45:11: And Ebed-melech took the men and went into the underground house of the king, and took from there old rags and old ropes, and threw them to Jeremiah into the cistern,
verses.45:12: and said, "Put these underneath the ropes." And Jeremiah did so.
verses.45:13: And they pulled him with the ropes and brought him up out of the cistern; and Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard.
verses.45:14: And the king sent and called him to himself into the house of Haseleisel, which is in the house of the Lord. And the king said to him, "I will ask you a question, and please do not hide a word from me."
verses.45:15: And Jeremiah said to the king, "If I tell you, will you not certainly put me to death? And if I give you counsel, you will certainly not listen to me."
verses.45:16: And the king swore to him, saying, "As the Lord lives, who made this life for us, I will certainly not kill you, and I will not give you into the hands of these men."
verses.45:17: And Jeremiah said to him, "Thus says the Lord: 'If you indeed go out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, your soul will live, and this city will certainly not be burned down with fire, and you and your household will live.
verses.45:18: And if you do not go out, this city will be given into the hands of the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with fire, and you will certainly not be saved.'"
verses.45:19: And the king said to Jeremiah, "I am concerned about the Judeans who have fled to the Chaldeans, that they might give me into their hands, and they will mock me."
verses.45:20: And Jeremiah said, "They will certainly not hand you over. Listen to the word of the Lord that I am speaking to you, and it will be better for you, and your soul will live.
verses.45:21: And if you are not willing to go out, this is the word that the Lord has shown me:
verses.45:22: And look, all the women who were left in the house of the king of Judah were being led out to the officials of the king of Babylon, and they were saying, 'Your men of peace have deceived you and will prevail over you; and they will bring down your feet in slippery places; they have turned away from you.'
verses.45:23: And they will bring out your wives and your children to the Chaldeans, and you will certainly not be saved, for you will be captured by the hand of the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned down."
verses.45:24: And the king said to him, "Let no one know any of these words, and you will certainly not die.
verses.45:25: And if the officials hear that I have spoken to you, and they come to you and say to you, 'Tell us, what did the king speak to you? Do not hide it from us, and we will certainly not put you to death; and what did the king speak to you?'
verses.45:26: then you will say to them, 'I am casting my mercy before the eyes of the king, so that he will not send me back to the house of Jonathan to die there.'"
verses.45:27: And all the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him; and he told them according to all these words that the king had commanded him; and they fell silent, because the word of the Lord was not heard.
verses.45:28: And Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard until the time when Jerusalem was captured.
verses.46:1: And it came about in the ninth month of Zedekiah king of Judah that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came against Jerusalem, and they were besieging it.
verses.46:2: And in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth of the month, the city was breached.
verses.46:3: And all the leaders of the king of Babylon entered and sat in the Middle Gate: Marganasar, and Samagoth, and Nabusachar, and Nabusaris, Nagargasnaser, Rabamath, and the rest of the commanders of the king of Babylon.
verses.46:14: And they sent and took Jeremiah out of the court of the guard, and gave him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, and they brought him out, and he remained among the people.
verses.46:15: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in the court of the guard, saying,
verses.46:16: "Go and say to Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, 'Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Look, I am bringing My words upon this city for evil and not for good,
verses.46:17: and I will save you on that day, and I will certainly not give you into the hands of the men whose presence you fear.
verses.46:18: For I will certainly save you, and by the sword you will certainly not fall; and your life will be as a find, because you trusted in Me,'" says the Lord.
verses.47:1: The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah after Nebuzaradan the chief cook from Daman had sent him away, when he took him in shackles among the exiles of Judah who had been led to Babylon.
verses.47:2: And the chief cook took him and said to him, "The Lord your God spoke these evils against this place,
verses.47:3: and the Lord has done it, because you sinned against Him and did not listen to His voice.
verses.47:4: Look, I have released you from the shackles that are on your hands. If it is good in your sight to come with me to Babylon, then I will set my eyes upon you;
verses.47:5: but if not, go away, return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed in the land of Judah, and live with him among the people in the land of Judah; to all the places that are good in your eyes to go, go." And the chief cook gave him gifts and sent him away.
verses.47:6: And he came to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and remained among the people who were left in the land.
verses.47:7: And all the commanders of the army that was in the field, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah in the land, and they had entrusted to him men and their wives whom he had not exiled to Babylon.
verses.47:8: And there came to Gedaliah at Mizpah Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and Johanan son of Kareah, and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Jophe the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.
verses.47:9: And Gedaliah swore to them and to their men, saying, "Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans; dwell in the land and work for the king of Babylon, and it will be better for you.
verses.47:10: And look, I am staying before you at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who may come to you; and as for you, gather wine and summer fruit and oil, and put them into your vessels, and live in the cities that you have occupied."
verses.47:11: And all the Judeans who were in Moab and among the sons of Ammon and those in Idumea and those in all the land heard that the king of Babylon had given a remnant to Judah, and that he had appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam.
verses.47:12: And they came to Gedaliah in the land of Judah, to Mizpah, and they gathered wine and very much summer fruit and oil.
verses.47:13: And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the army who were in the fields came to Gedaliah at Mizpah
verses.47:14: and said to him, "Do you indeed know that Belisa king of the sons of Ammon has sent Ishmael to you to strike your life?" And Gedaliah did not believe them.
verses.47:15: And Johanan said to Gedaliah secretly in Mizpah, "Let me go now and strike down Ishmael, and let no one know, so that he may not strike your life, and all Judah who have been gathered to you be scattered, and the rest of Judah perish."
verses.47:16: And Gedaliah said to Johanan, "Do not do this thing, for you are speaking lies concerning Ishmael."
verses.48:1: And it happened in the seventh month that Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elasa, from the lineage of the king, and ten men with him, came to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and they ate bread there together.
verses.48:2: And Ishmael and the ten men who were with him rose up and struck down Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land,
verses.48:3: and all the Judeans who were with him in Mizpah and all the Chaldeans who were found there.
verses.48:4: And it happened on the second day after he had struck down Gedaliah, while no one knew,
verses.48:5: that men came from Shechem and from Salem and from Samaria, eighty men, with their beards shaved and their garments torn and beating themselves, with manna and frankincense in their hands to bring into the house of the Lord.
verses.48:6: And Ishmael went out to meet them; they were going along and weeping, and he said to them, "Come in to Gedaliah."
verses.48:7: And it happened, when they had entered into the middle of the city, that he slaughtered them into the cistern.
verses.48:8: And ten men were found there and said to Ishmael, "Do not kill us, for we have stores in the field—wheat and barley, honey and oil." And he passed by and did not kill them in the midst of their brothers.
verses.48:9: And the cistern into which Ishmael threw all whom he had struck down—this is a great cistern that King Asa made because of Baasha king of Israel—this Ishmael filled with those struck down.
verses.48:10: And Ishmael turned back all the people who were left in Mizpah and the daughters of the king whom the chief cook had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, and he departed to the other side of the sons of Ammon.
verses.48:11: And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the force who were with him heard all the evil things that Ishmael had done,
verses.48:12: and they led their entire army and departed to fight against him, and they found him by much water in Gibeon.
verses.48:13: And it happened, when all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan and the commanders of the force that was with him,
verses.48:14: that they turned back to Johanan.
verses.48:15: And Ishmael escaped with eight men and departed to the sons of Ammon.
verses.48:16: And Johanan and all the commanders of the force who were with him took all the remnant of the people whom he had brought back from Ishmael—mighty men in war, and the women, and the rest, and the eunuchs whom he had brought back from Gibeon—
verses.48:17: and they departed and stayed in Gaberochamaa, which is near Bethlehem, to go into Egypt
verses.48:18: because of the Chaldeans, for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael had struck down Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon had appointed in the land.
verses.49:1: And all the commanders of the force, and Johanan, and Azariah son of Maaseiah, and all the people from the least even to the greatest came near
verses.49:2: to Jeremiah the prophet and said to him, "Please let our mercy fall before your face, and pray to the Lord your God for this remnant, for we have been left few out of many, just as your eyes see.
verses.49:3: And let the Lord your God tell us the way in which we should go and the thing that we should do."
verses.49:4: And Jeremiah said to them, "I have heard; look, I will pray to the Lord our God according to your words. And it will be, whatever word the Lord answers, I will tell you; I will by no means hide a word from you."
verses.49:5: And they said to Jeremiah, "May the Lord be a righteous and faithful witness among us, if according to every word that the Lord sends to us we do not do so.
verses.49:6: Whether good or evil, we will listen to the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may be better for us, because we will listen to the voice of the Lord our God."
verses.49:7: And it happened after ten days that the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah.
verses.49:8: And he called Johanan and the commanders of the force and all the people from the least even to the greatest,
verses.49:9: and said to them, "Thus says the Lord:
verses.49:10: 'If you indeed stay in this land, I will build you up and will by no means tear down, and I will plant you and will by no means uproot, for I have ceased from the evils that I did to you.
verses.49:11: Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom you are afraid; do not be afraid, says the Lord, for I am with you to deliver you and to save you from their hand.
verses.49:12: And I will give you mercy, and I will have mercy on you and return you to your land.'
verses.49:13: And if you say, 'We will by no means stay in this land,' so as not to listen to the voice of the Lord,
verses.49:14: 'for we will enter into the land of Egypt, and we will by no means see war, and we will by no means hear the sound of a trumpet, and we will by no means be hungry for bread, and there we will dwell'—
verses.49:15: therefore hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord: 'If you set your face toward Egypt and enter there to dwell,
verses.49:16: then it will be that the sword of which you are afraid will find you in the land of Egypt, and the famine about which you are concerned will overtake you behind you in Egypt, and there you will die.
verses.49:17: And it will be that all the people and all the foreigners who set their face toward the land of Egypt to dwell there will perish by the sword and by the famine, and there will be no one of them escaping from the evils that I am bringing upon them.'
verses.49:18: For thus says the Lord: 'Just as My wrath poured down upon those who dwell in Jerusalem, so My wrath will pour down upon you when you enter into Egypt; and you will become a desolation, and subjugated, and a curse, and a reproach, and you will by no means see this place any longer.'
verses.49:19: What the Lord has spoken concerning you, the remnant of Judah, is, 'Do not enter into Egypt.' And now you will certainly know
verses.49:20: that you have acted wickedly in your souls when you sent me, saying, 'Pray for us to the Lord,' and, 'According to all that the Lord speaks to you, we will do.'
verses.49:21: And you did not listen to the voice of the Lord, with which He sent me to you.
verses.49:22: And now by sword and by famine you will perish in the place where you desire to enter to dwell."
verses.50:1: And it happened, when Jeremiah finished speaking to the people all the words of the Lord with which the Lord had sent him to them, all these words,
verses.50:2: that Azariah son of Maaseiah and Johanan son of Kareah and all the men who addressed Jeremiah spoke, saying, "You are lying! The Lord has not sent you to us, saying, 'Do not enter into Egypt to dwell there,'
verses.50:3: but rather Baruch son of Neriah is inciting you against us, so that you may give us into the hands of the Chaldeans to put us to death and for us to be exiled to Babylon."
verses.50:4: And Johanan and all the commanders of the force and all the people did not listen to the voice of the Lord, to dwell in the land of Judah.
verses.50:5: And Johanan and all the commanders of the force took all the remnant of Judah who had returned to dwell in the land,
verses.50:6: the mighty men and the women and the rest and the daughters of the king, and the souls whom Nebuzaradan had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, and Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah,
verses.50:7: and they entered into Egypt, because they did not listen to the voice of the Lord, and they entered into Tahpanhes.
verses.50:8: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
verses.50:9: "Take for yourself large stones and hide them in the entranceway, at the gate of the house of Pharaoh in Tahpanhes, before the eyes of men of Judah,
verses.50:10: and you will say, 'Thus says the Lord: Look, I am sending and will bring Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will set his throne over these stones that you hid, and he will lift up weapons against them,
verses.50:11: and he will enter and strike the land of Egypt: those for death, to death, and those for exile, to exile, and those for the sword, to the sword;
verses.50:12: and he will kindle a fire in the houses of their gods, and he will burn them up and take them into exile, and he will delouse the land of Egypt just as a shepherd delouses his garment. And he will go out in peace,
verses.50:13: and he will shatter the pillars of Heliopolis that are in On, and he will burn up their houses with fire.'"
verses.51:1: The word that came to Jeremiah for all the Jews who were dwelling in the land of Egypt, and those residing in Migdol and in Tahpanhes and in the land of Pathros, saying:
verses.51:2: Thus said the Lord, the God of Israel: "You have seen all the evils that I brought upon Jerusalem and upon the cities of Judah; and look, they are desolate, without inhabitants,
verses.51:3: because of their wickedness that they committed to provoke Me, going to burn incense to other gods whom you did not know.
verses.51:4: And I sent to you My servants the prophets at dawn, and I sent them, saying, 'Do not do this thing of defilement that I have hated.'
verses.51:5: And they did not listen and did not incline their ear to turn away from their evils, so as not to burn incense to other gods.
verses.51:6: And My wrath and My fury poured down and blazed up in the gates of Judah and outside Jerusalem, and they became a desolation and an untrodden place, as it is this day."
verses.51:7: And now, thus said the Lord Almighty: "Why are you doing great evils against your own souls, to cut off from you man and woman, infant and nursing child from the midst of Judah, so that none of you is left,
verses.51:8: provoking Me by the works of your hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt, into which you came to dwell, so that you may be cut off and become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?
verses.51:9: Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers, and the evils of the kings of Judah, and the evils of your rulers, and the evils of your wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and outside Jerusalem?
verses.51:10: And they have not ceased to this day, and they did not hold fast to My ordinances that I set before their fathers."
verses.51:11: Therefore, thus said the Lord: "Look, I am setting My face
verses.51:12: to destroy all the remnant who are in Egypt, and they will fall by sword and by famine, and they will perish from the least to the greatest, and they will become a reproach and a destruction and a curse.
verses.51:13: And I will call to account those residing in the land of Egypt, just as I called Jerusalem to account, by sword and by famine,
verses.51:14: and there will be no one saved from the remainder of Judah who are sojourning in the land of Egypt to return to the land of Judah, for which they themselves hope in their souls, to return there; they will by no means return, except those who are rescued."
verses.51:15: And all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense answered Jeremiah, and all the women, a great assembly, and all the people residing in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, saying:
verses.51:16: "As for the word that you spoke to us in the name of the Lord, we will not listen to you;
verses.51:17: for we will surely do every word that will go out from our mouth, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her, just as we and our fathers and our kings and our rulers did in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem; and we were filled with bread, and we were well off, and we saw no evils.
verses.51:18: And since we stopped burning incense to the queen of heaven, we were all diminished, and by sword and by famine we perished.
verses.51:19: And since we burn incense to the queen of heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes for her and pour out drink offerings to her without our husbands?"
verses.51:20: And Jeremiah said to all the people, to the mighty men and to the women, and to all the people who had answered him with words, saying:
verses.51:21: "Did not the Lord remember the incense that we burned in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem—you and your fathers and your kings and your rulers and the people of the land—and did it not come up into His heart?
verses.51:22: And the Lord could no longer bear it because of the wickedness of your deeds and because of the abominations that you committed; and your land became a desolation and an untrodden place and a curse, as on this day,
verses.51:23: because of what you burned as incense and how you sinned against the Lord; and you did not listen to the voice of the Lord, and you did not walk in His ordinances and in the law and in His testimonies, and these evils overtook you."
verses.51:24: And Jeremiah said to the people and to the women, "Hear the word of the Lord."
verses.51:25: Thus said the Lord, the God of Israel: "You women spoke with your mouth and fulfilled it with your hands, saying, 'We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her.' You surely stood by your vows, and you surely performed them."
verses.51:26: Therefore, hear the word of the Lord, all Judah who reside in the land of Egypt: "Look, I have sworn by My great name," said the Lord, "that My name will no longer be in the mouth of anyone of Judah to say, 'The Lord lives,' in all the land of Egypt.
verses.51:27: For I am keeping watch over them to harm them and not to do them good; and all Judah who dwell in the land of Egypt will perish by sword and by famine, if they come to an end.
verses.51:28: And those saved from the sword will return to the land of Judah, few in number; and the remnant of Judah who settled in the land of Egypt to dwell there will know whose word will stand.
verses.51:29: And this is the sign to you that I Myself will call you to account for harm."
verses.51:30: Thus said the Lord: "Look, I am giving Hophra king of Egypt into the hands of his enemy and into the hands of those seeking his life, just as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy and the one seeking his life."
verses.51:31: The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah, when he was writing these words in the book from the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
verses.51:32: Thus said the Lord concerning you, Baruch,
verses.51:33: because you said, "Woe is me, woe is me! For the Lord has added trouble to my pain; I lay down in groanings; I found no rest";
verses.51:34: say to him, "Thus said the Lord: 'Look, those whom I built, I am tearing down; and those whom I planted, I am uprooting.
verses.51:35: And will you seek great things for yourself? Do not seek them; for look, I am bringing evils upon all flesh,' says the Lord, 'and I will give your life as a find in every place where you may walk.'"
verses.52:1: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
verses.52:4: And it happened in the ninth year of his reign, in the ninth month, on the tenth of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came against Jerusalem, and they surrounded it with a palisade and built four-footed siegeworks all around it.
verses.52:5: And the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah,
verses.52:6: on the ninth of the month; and the famine grew severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.
verses.52:7: And the city was breached, and all the men of war went out by night by the way of the gate between the wall and the outer wall, which was by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were all around the city. And they went by the way to the Arabah,
verses.52:8: and the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and they overtook him on the far side of Jericho, and all his servants were scattered from him.
verses.52:9: And they captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Deblatha, and he spoke to him with judgment.
verses.52:10: And the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and he slaughtered all the rulers of Judah in Deblatha.
verses.52:11: And he blinded the eyes of Zedekiah and bound him in fetters; and the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him in a millhouse until the day he died.
verses.52:12: And in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month, Nebuzaradan the chief cook, who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem,
verses.52:13: and he burned the house of the Lord and the house of the king, and all the houses of the city and every great house he burned with fire.
verses.52:14: And the army of the Chaldeans that was with the chief cook tore down every wall of Jerusalem all around.
verses.52:16: And the chief cook left the remnant of the people as vinedressers and as farmers.
verses.52:17: And the Chaldeans broke in pieces the bronze pillars that were in the house of the Lord, and the stands, and the bronze sea that was in the house of the Lord, and they took their bronze and carried it away to Babylon.
verses.52:18: And the rim, and the bowls, and the meat forks, and all the bronze vessels with which they ministered,
verses.52:19: and the sapphoth, and the masmaroth, and the pouring vessels, and the lampstands, and the censers, and the ladles—whatever was gold as gold and whatever was silver as silver—the chief cook took.
verses.52:20: And the two pillars, and the one sea, and the twelve bronze calves beneath the sea, which King Solomon made for the house of the Lord—there was no weighing of their bronze.
verses.52:21: And as for the pillars, the height of the one pillar was thirty-five cubits, and a cord of twelve cubits encircled it, and its thickness was four fingers all around,
verses.52:22: and a bronze capital was upon them, and five cubits was the length, the height of the one capital, and network and pomegranates were upon the capital all around, all of bronze; and it was the same for the second pillar: eight pomegranates to the cubit for the twelve cubits.
verses.52:23: And the pomegranates were ninety-six on one side, and all the pomegranates were one hundred upon the network all around.
verses.52:24: And the chief cook took the first priest and the second priest and the three who guarded the way,
verses.52:25: and one eunuch who was overseer of the men of war, and seven renowned men who were in the presence of the king, who were found in the city, and the scribe of the armies who served as scribe for the people of the land, and sixty men from the people of the land who were found in the midst of the city.
verses.52:26: And Nebuzaradan the chief cook took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Deblatha;
verses.52:27: and the king of Babylon struck them down in Deblatha in the land of Hamath.
verses.52:31: And it happened in the thirty-seventh year after Jehoiakim king of Judah was taken into exile, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fourth of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year in which he became king, lifted up the head of Jehoiakim king of Judah and cut his hair, and brought him out of the house where he was guarded,
verses.52:32: and spoke kindly to him, and set his throne above the kings who were with him in Babylon,
verses.52:33: and they changed his prison garment, and he ate bread continually before him all the days that he lived.
verses.52:34: And his allowance was given to him continually from the king of Babylon, from day to day, until the day he died.

notes.1:1: The Septuagint opens with "The word of God that came upon Jeremiah," whereas the Hebrew MT begins "The words of Jeremiah."
notes.1:2: The Greek reads "Amos" (Ἀμώς) rather than MT "Amon." The relative clause literally reads "which word of God came to him," reflecting a Semitic resumptive pronoun construction.
notes.1:5: The Greek uses the present tense "I know" (ἐπίσταμαι) alongside the perfects "I have sanctified" and "I have set," and omits "from the womb" after "before you came out."
notes.1:6: The Greek translates the Hebrew exclamation 'ahah ("Ah!") as the divine title "One Who Is" (Ὁ ὤν), echoing Exodus 3:14.
notes.1:11: Greek καρυίνην literally means "of a nut tree" (walnut or almond), rendering Hebrew shaqed ("almond"), whose wordplay with shoqed ("watching") in v. 12 is not preserved in Greek.
notes.2:2: The Septuagint omits MT 2:1–2a and diverges sharply here, reading "the love of his perfection" (τελειώσεως αὐτοῦ) and "the Holy One of Israel" where MT refers to bridal devotion in the wilderness.
notes.2:7: The Greek renders Hebrew ha-karmel ("the fruitful land") as the proper name "Carmel" (τὸν Κάρμηλον).
notes.2:8: Here and in vv. 23 and 28, the Greek uses the feminine article with Baal (τῇ Βάαλ), reflecting the practice of reading Hebrew boshet ("shame," feminine) in place of Baal.
notes.2:18: The Greek uses the river name "Gihon" (Γηών, cf. Gen 2:13) where MT has "Shihor" (the Nile), and plural "rivers" where MT has singular "the River" (the Euphrates).
notes.2:23: Verses 23–24 differ substantially from MT, reading "in the burial ground" (πολυανδρίῳ, MT "in the valley"), "at evening her voice wailed," "she was carried along by the wind," and "in her humiliation" (v. 24, MT "in her month").
notes.3:1: The Greek text differs from the Hebrew in several notable details: the woman (rather than the husband) is the subject of 'return,' 'that woman' replaces 'that land,' 'shepherds' replaces 'lovers/companions' (as also in 3:3), and the final clause is an imperfect question ('were you returning to Me?') rather than an imperative.
notes.3:3: The Greek reads 'many shepherds as a stumbling block to yourself' (cf. 3:2 'deserted crow'), diverging markedly from the Hebrew text's imagery of withheld showers and an Arab in the wilderness.
notes.3:6: Greek 'dwelling' (katoikia) here and in 3:8, 12 reflects a Septuagint reading of the Hebrew term for 'backsliding' as derived from the root 'to dwell.'
notes.3:8: The Greek text preserves an ancient repetition ('on account of all the things that I also saw, on account of all the things in which...') found in major Septuagint witnesses.
notes.3:19: The Greek begins with 'May it be so, Lord!' before shifting abruptly to God speaking ('For I will set you among nations... an inheritance of God Almighty of nations'), diverging substantially from the Hebrew ('How I would set you among sons').
notes.4:1: The Greek reads 'from his mouth' (rather than Hebrew 'from before Me') and 'before the presence' without a possessive pronoun ('My'), followed by 'stands in awe' (eulabethe).
notes.4:11: Greek pneuma can mean either 'spirit' or 'wind.' In 4:11-12 the Septuagint renders the Hebrew winnowing-wind imagery as 'a spirit of error in the wilderness,' 'not for what is pure nor for what is holy,' and 'a spirit of fullness.'
notes.4:20: The Greek places two accusative nouns ('ruin, destruction') directly with the verb epikaleitai ('calls upon'), a compressed and unusual Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew.
notes.4:23: The Greek condenses the Hebrew phrase 'formless and void' (cf. Gen 1:2) to the single stark word 'nothing' (outhen).
notes.4:26: The Greek treats Hebrew hak-karmel ('the fruitful land/orchard') as the proper place name 'Carmel,' and reads 'burned with fire' rather than 'torn down.'
notes.5:6: The Greek reads "a wolf as far as the houses" (ἕως τῶν οἰκιῶν), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "a wolf of the deserts" (or "of the evenings").
notes.5:10: The Greek commands to "leave behind her supports, for they belong to the Lord," contrasting sharply with the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("strip away her branches, for they are not the Lord's").
notes.5:11: In the Greek syntax, "the house of Israel" is the subject of the verb in 5:11 while "the house of Judah" serves as the singular subject of "lied" (ἐψεύσατο) at the beginning of 5:12.
notes.5:31: The Greek reads "the priests clapped with their hands" (ἐπεκρότησαν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτῶν), picturing approval of the prophets, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the priests rule at their direction."
notes.6:1: The Greek renders the opening imperative as "Be strong" (ἐνισχύσατε) rather than "Flee for safety" as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text; "Beth-hakkerem" translates Greek Βαιθθαχαρμά.
notes.6:11: In the Greek, the Lord Himself speaks throughout 6:11 ("I filled up My wrath... I will pour it out"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the prophet speaking of being full of the Lord's wrath before a command to pour it out.
notes.6:16: The Greek promises "purification" (ἁγνισμόν) for their souls, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text promises "rest."
notes.6:18: The Greek renders this as a past statement ("Therefore the nations heard, and those who shepherd their flocks") rather than an imperative call to the nations and congregation as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.6:27: The Greek reads "among tested peoples, and you will know Me when I test their way," repeating the root for testing (δοκιμ-) and making the Lord the one who tests their way, unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.7:2: The Greek text begins this oracle directly at 7:2 without the temple-gate narrative of the Hebrew Masoretic Text (7:1-2a), and addresses Judea rather than Judah.
notes.7:4: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the Greek adds "in yourselves" and "for they will not benefit you at all," and repeats "the temple of the Lord" twice rather than three times.
notes.7:10: The Greek reads "We have refrained from doing all these abominations" (a hypocritical claim of innocence), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "We are delivered—to do all these abominations."
notes.7:18: The Greek identifies the recipient of the sacrificial cakes as "the host of heaven" rather than "the queen of heaven" as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.7:29: The Greek reads "on your lips" rather than "on the bare heights," and "the generation that does these things" rather than "the generation of His wrath."
notes.8:2: The Greek reads "dry them out," "will not be mourned," and "an example" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "spread them out," "will not be gathered," and "like dung."
notes.8:6: The Greek opens with plural imperatives and closes with "the runner has ceased from his course, like a horse drenched in sweat in its neighing," differing markedly from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.8:7: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew term for stork as asida, and lists "swallow of the field, sparrows" where the Hebrew lists swallow and crane.
notes.8:10: Verses 8:10b-12 of the Hebrew Masoretic Text (parallel to 6:12-15) are absent from the Greek text, which continues directly from 8:10 into 8:13.
notes.8:18: In the Greek text, 8:18 completes the Lord's sentence begun in 8:17 ("they will bite you incurably with pain, while your heart is perplexed") rather than beginning the prophet's lament as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.9:4: Greek reads "did not cease so as to turn back" and opens 9:5 with "Usury upon usury," diverging from the Hebrew MT ("they weary themselves committing iniquity; your dwelling is in the midst of deceit").
notes.9:9: Greek reads "the sound of possessions" where MT has "the sound of livestock," and in 9:10 reads "deportation" and "dragons" where MT has "heaps of ruins" and "jackals."
notes.9:21: Greek reads "as an example" and "grass" where MT has "like dung" and "sheaves," and lacks the introductory speech formula found at the start of MT 9:22.
notes.9:25: Greek lists "Idumea" (Idoumaia) alongside "Edom" where MT has "Judah" alongside "Edom," and explicitly adds "in flesh" in contrast to 9:24 ("circumcised in their foreskins").
notes.10:9: This Greek text has no verses 10:6-8 or 10:10 (present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text) and preserves the Greek place-name 'Mophaz' where the Hebrew has 'Uphaz.'
notes.10:13: Greek lacks the opening clause of MT ("when He utters His voice") and reads "light" brought out from God's storehouses where MT reads "wind."
notes.10:17: Greek has a third-person past statement ("He has gathered your substance from outside") and "in choice places," whereas MT has a second-person imperative ("Gather up your bundle from the ground") and "under siege."
notes.10:19: Greek uses second-person pronouns throughout 10:19 and the opening of 10:20 ("your shattering... your wound... your injury"), shifting to first person in 10:20 where it also reads "my sheep" and "a place for my tent, a place for my curtains."
notes.10:24: Greek reads first-person plural "us" twice where MT has singular "me."
notes.11:6: Greek reads "Read aloud" and "outside Jerusalem" where MT has "Proclaim" and "in the streets of Jerusalem," omits MT 11:7, and retains only the brief clause in 11:8.
notes.11:13: Greek places the feminine article before Baal (also in 11:17), a Septuagint convention reflecting the oral substitution of the feminine noun "shame" (Hebrew bosheth) for the deity's name.
notes.11:16: Greek reads "at the sound of its circumcision," deriving the Hebrew word for "tumult" from the root meaning "to circumcise," and adds "great is the affliction upon you."
notes.11:19: Greek reads "let us cast wood into his bread" where the Hebrew MT reads "let us destroy the tree with its fruit" (literally "its bread").
notes.11:21: Greek reads first-person "my life" (in Jeremiah's voice) where MT has second-person "your life," and omits the renewed messenger formula at the opening of MT 11:22.
notes.12:2: Greek reads "they bore children" (ἐτεκνοποιήσαντο) rather than the Hebrew MT "they grow/go on"; "kidneys" (νεφρῶν) is a biblical idiom for the innermost mind and affections.
notes.12:3: Greek ἅγνισον ("purify" or "consecrate") omits the Hebrew MT's preceding clause "drag them out like sheep for slaughter" while rendering the verb for setting apart.
notes.12:5: Greek reads "Your feet run" (σοῦ οἱ πόδες τρέχουσιν) and "you are not confident" (οὐ πέποιθας), differing from Hebrew MT ("you have run with footmen" and "you feel safe"); "roaring" translates φρύαγμα (lit. snorting, insolent roaring).
notes.12:9: Greek reads "a hyena's cave ... or a cave around it" (σπήλαιον ὑαίνης ... ἢ σπήλαιον κύκλῳ αὐτῆς), diverging notably from the Hebrew MT ("a speckled bird of prey").
notes.12:12: Greek reads only "from the end of the land" (ἀπ᾽ ἄκρου τῆς γῆς), omitting the Hebrew MT's continuation "even to the other end of the land."
notes.13:14: Greek reads "I will scatter them" (διασκορπιῶ) and "I will not yearn" (οὐκ ἐπιποθήσω), whereas the Hebrew MT reads "I will dash them one against another" and "I will not pity."
notes.13:17: Greek attributes the weeping soul and eyes to the people ("your soul ... your eyes") and reads "has been crushed" (συνετρίβη), whereas the Hebrew MT has "my soul ... my eye" and "has been taken captive."
notes.13:18: Greek addresses "those who rule" (τοῖς δυναστεύουσιν) rather than the Hebrew MT's "queen mother."
notes.13:22: Greek τὰ ὀπίσθιά σου ("your back parts"; cf. τὰ ὀπίσω σου in 13:26) renders a Hebrew term for skirts or lower garments, conveying public exposure and disgrace.
notes.14:2: Greek uses "Judea" (ἡ Ἰουδαία) here—distinct from "Judah" (Ἰούδας, as in 14:19)—and reads "her gates were emptied" (ἐκενώθησαν) rather than the Hebrew MT "languish."
notes.14:8: Greek reads "like a native" (ὡς αὐτόχθων) rather than the Hebrew MT "like a traveler," contrasting sharply with "sojourner" (πάροικος); "Hope" renders ὑπομονή ("patient waiting, endurance, expectation").
notes.14:10: Greek reads "God has not prospered in them" (ὁ θεὸς οὐκ εὐόδωσεν ἐν αὐτοῖς, rather than εὐδοκέω "be pleased with" as in 14:12) and omits the Hebrew MT's closing clause "and He will punish their sins."
notes.14:13: Greek "O One Who Is, Lord" (Ὁ ὤν, Κύριε) echoes the divine title of Exodus 3:14 LXX, rendering the Hebrew exclamation "Alas, Lord God!"
notes.14:15: Greek reads "By a diseased death they will die" (Ἐν θανάτῳ νοσερῷ ἀποθανοῦνται), whereas the Hebrew MT reads "By sword and famine those prophets will meet their end."
notes.15:10: Greek reads "I neither gave benefit, nor did anyone benefit me; my strength failed among those who curse me," differing from the Hebrew MT ("I have not lent, nor have they lent to me; all of them curse me").
notes.15:11: In the Septuagint Jeremiah speaks here, addressing God as "Master" (despota) and protesting his intercession while his enemies prosper, whereas the Hebrew MT attributes this verse to the Lord.
notes.15:16: Greek reads "from those who reject Your words; bring an end to them," continuing the sentence from verse 15, where the Hebrew MT has "Your words were found, and I ate them."
notes.15:18: The feminine verb phrase refers back to Jeremiah's "wound" rather than addressing God directly ("You have become to me") as in the Hebrew MT.
notes.15:19: This Greek text reads axiou ("worthy") rather than anaxiou ("unworthy") or the Hebrew MT ("worthless").
notes.16:1: The Septuagint omits the introductory formula found in the Hebrew MT ("The word of the Lord came to me, saying") and opens directly with the Lord's command.
notes.16:4: Greek renders the Hebrew term for "dung" as paradeigma ("an example") and places the wild beasts and birds before the sword and famine.
notes.16:12: Greek ton areston ("the pleasing things") corresponds to "stubbornness" in the Hebrew MT.
notes.16:13: In the Septuagint the "other gods" are the subject of the final clause ("who will not give you mercy"), whereas the Hebrew MT has the Lord declaring that He will show no favor.
notes.16:18: The Septuagint lacks the Hebrew MT's "first" and "doubly," and reads "trespassed against" (eplemmelesan) where the MT has "filled."
notes.17:5: Verses 17:1-4 are absent from the Old Greek (Septuagint) text of Jeremiah, which begins the chapter here without the Hebrew MT's "Thus says the Lord."
notes.17:9: Greek reads "deep" (batheia) rather than "deceitful," and translates the Hebrew word for "incurable" as anthropos ("a man"), followed by the masculine pronoun "him."
notes.17:16: As in 17:9, Greek renders the Hebrew term for "woeful/incurable" as anthropou ("the day of man"), and reads "I did not grow weary following behind You" rather than the Hebrew MT's shepherd imagery.
notes.17:26: Greek transliterates Hebrew minhah ("grain offering") as manna and includes an additional offering term (thymiamata, "incenses").
notes.17:27: Greek amphoda ("streets" or "city blocks") corresponds to "citadels/palaces" in the Hebrew MT.
notes.18:3: Greek "on the stones" refers to the two stone disks of a potter's wheel. In 18:4 the Septuagint reads "fell" (epesen) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "was spoiled."
notes.18:7: The Greek adverbial peras ("in the end" or "finally," also in 18:9) corresponds to the Hebrew rega' ("at one moment" or "suddenly").
notes.18:12: The Septuagint reads "We will act courageously" (andrioumetha) and "our turnings away" where the Hebrew reads "It is hopeless" and "our plans."
notes.18:14: The Septuagint reads "breasts from a rock" (mastoi, reflecting a reading of the Hebrew word for "field" as "breasts") and "water carried violently by the wind," differing markedly from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.18:15: Greek schoinous aiōnious ("eternal cords," perhaps denoting boundary lines or tracks) stands where the Hebrew reads "ancient paths." In 18:18 the Septuagint also lacks a negative before "we will listen to all his words."
notes.19:2: Greek "burial ground" (polyandrion, also in 19:6) replaces Hebrew "valley," and "sons of their children" appears where the Hebrew has "Ben-Hinnom." The Septuagint's "Tharsis Gate" (pylēs tēs Tharseis) is a distinct Greek name corresponding to the Hebrew "Potsherd (Harsith) Gate."
notes.19:6: Greek Diaptōsis ("Collapse," also in 19:14, with the related participle "collapsing" in 19:12-13) renders the Hebrew place name "Topheth" as a descriptive noun of ruin.
notes.19:7: The Septuagint reads "I will slaughter" (sphaxō), creating a wordplay with "Burial Ground of the Slaughter" in 19:6, where the Hebrew reads "I will make void."
notes.19:15: The Septuagint concludes with "My commands" (tōn entolōn mou) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "my words."
notes.20:2: Greek kataraktēn ("dungeon" or "trapdoor cell," also in 20:3) corresponds to Hebrew "stocks," and "the upper house set apart" appears where the Hebrew names the "Upper Gate of Benjamin."
notes.20:3: Greek Metoikon ("Exile" or "Migrant") connects with "exile" (metoikian) and "they will exile" (metoikiousin) in 20:4, interpreting the Hebrew name Magor-missaviv ("Terror on every side") from the root meaning "to sojourn" or "migrate."
notes.20:8: The Septuagint reads "with my bitter word I will laugh" (linked to "laughter" in 20:7) where the Hebrew reads "whenever I speak, I cry out."
notes.20:10: The Septuagint renders Hebrew "terror on every side" as "gathering together all around, all around" and makes the call to watch Jeremiah's "intention" a direct command addressed to his friends.
notes.20:11: The Septuagint reads "they pursued and were unable to understand" where the Hebrew reads "my persecutors will stumble and will not prevail."
notes.21:1: The Greek reads Manassaiou (Manassaeus), differing from the Hebrew Maaseiah.
notes.21:6: Greek thanatos ("death") is the Septuagint's regular rendering for deadly pestilence (so also in 21:7).
notes.21:7: Unlike the Hebrew, the Greek omits Nebuchadnezzar here, makes the enemies the plural subject of "they will cut them down," and attributes the refusal to spare directly to the Lord in the first person.
notes.21:13: The Greek transliterates Hebrew tsur ("rock") as the proper name Sor and reads "terrify" instead of "come down against"; in 21:14 the Greek also omits the opening clause found in the Hebrew.
notes.22:6: The Greek conditional ean me ("if I do not...") represents a Hebrew oath formula expressing emphatic certainty ("surely I will...").
notes.22:13: The Greek lacks "Woe to" at the opening and renders the Hebrew idiom for exacting unpaid labor from a neighbor literally as "will work with his neighbor for nothing."
notes.22:15: Where the Hebrew reads "competing in cedar; did not your father eat and drink?", the Greek reads "against Ahaz your father" and shifts to negative statements ("They will not eat and they will not drink"), continuing with negative verbs in 22:16 ("they did not judge... your not knowing Me").
notes.22:20: Where the Hebrew has the place name Abarim, the Greek translates the term as "the far side of the sea"; in 22:21-22 it also reads "in your transgression" (Hebrew: "in your prosperity") and "all those who love you" (Hebrew: "all your wickedness").
notes.22:28: Unlike the Hebrew's rhetorical questions about Coniah and his offspring, the Greek makes a statement about Jeconiah alone, and in 22:30 calls him ekkerykton ("an outcast/banished man") rather than "childless."
notes.23:6: Greek reads "which the Lord will call him: Josedek," treating the Hebrew title ("the Lord is our righteousness") as a proper name, and closes the verse with the superscription "Concerning the prophets" (literally "Among the prophets"), which introduces verse 9 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.23:10: Greek reads "their forest" (drymos), likely an early scribal shift from dromos ("course"), and omits the negation in the final clause ("and their strength likewise," versus Hebrew "and their might is not right").
notes.23:31: Greek reads "and slumber their slumber," interpreting the Hebrew verb ("utter an oracle") from the root meaning "to slumber."
notes.23:33: Greek lemma means "burden" or "what is taken up" (used for a prophetic oracle), preparing for the wordplay on lambano ("taking you up") in verse 39; Greek also reads "You are the burden" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "What burden?"
notes.23:40: In this Greek text the words that the Hebrew Masoretic Text has at 23:7-8 follow the threat of everlasting reproach within verse 40 (there are no separate verses 7-8), and it reads 'and restored them to their land' where the Hebrew reads 'and they shall dwell on their own soil.'
notes.24:1: Greek reads "the prisoners" (where the Hebrew has "the smiths") and "the neighbors" (plesious; some Septuagint manuscripts read plousious, "the rich," a phrase absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text).
notes.24:9: Greek reads "to scattering" (where the Hebrew has "a horror") and uses the past tense "where I drove them out."
notes.24:10: Greek orders the triad as "famine and death and the sword," rendering the Hebrew term for "pestilence" literally as "death" (thanatos).
notes.25:3: Greek reads "Amos" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Amon" as the father of Josiah.
notes.25:9: Here and in verses 11-12, the Septuagint has a shorter text that refers to "a clan from the north" and "that nation" without naming Nebuchadnezzar or Babylon.
notes.25:10: Greek reads "the scent of perfume" (osmen myrou) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the sound of the millstones."
notes.25:14: In the Septuagint arrangement of Jeremiah, the Oracles Against the Nations begin here with Elam (corresponding to 49:34-39 in the Hebrew text), and the Greek phrase "of Elam" (ta Ailam) is sometimes punctuated as a separate subheading ("The matters concerning Elam").
notes.25:17: Greek reads "according to" (kata) rather than "disaster" (kaka), omitting an explicit direct object before "the wrath of My fury."
notes.26:2: Jeremiah 26:2-28 in the Septuagint corresponds to Jeremiah 46:2-28 in the Hebrew Bible (there is no verse 26:1 in the Greek text; Septuagint Jeremiah places the Oracles Against the Nations in chapters 25:14-31, corresponding to Hebrew chapters 46-51).
notes.26:14: Greek σμίλαξ ("bindweed" or "yew") is a Septuagint rendering distinct from the Hebrew "your surroundings."
notes.26:15: The Septuagint explicitly names Apis (ὁ Ἆπις), the sacred bull deity of Memphis, whereas the Hebrew reads "your mighty ones" (or "your mighty one").
notes.26:16: Greek μαχαίρας Ἑλληνικῆς ("the Greek sword") reflects the Septuagint reading of the Hebrew term for "oppressing" (hayyonah) as "Greece" (Yavan), a rendering repeated in 27:16.
notes.26:17: "Saon Esbei Emoed" (Σαὼν Ἑσβεὶ Ἑμωήδ) is the Septuagint transliteration as a proper name of the Hebrew phrase meaning "Noise, he has let the appointed time pass."
notes.26:28: The clause "the fearless and delicate one has been delivered up" (ἡ ἀπτόητος καὶ τρυφερὰ παρεδόθη) is a Septuagint-specific reading closely paralleling 27:2.
notes.27:1: Jeremiah 27 in the Septuagint corresponds to Jeremiah 50 in the Hebrew Bible.
notes.27:2: The Septuagint describes Bel as "the fearless one" (ἡ ἀπτόητος) and Merodach (Greek Μαιωδάκ) as "the delicate one" delivered up, differing markedly from the Hebrew text and echoing 26:28.
notes.27:8: Greek δράκοντες ("dragons") differs from the Hebrew "male goats" leading the flock.
notes.27:18: The adopted Greek text reads epi ton Babylonos ("on the one of Babylon"), omitting the noun basilea ("king") before Babylon.
notes.27:24: Greek ὡς Βαβυλών ("like Babylon") is translated literally; it likely arose within Greek transmission from vocative ὦ Βαβυλών ("O Babylon").
notes.27:38: The Septuagint links "upon her water" to the preceding verse ("scattered") and reads "put to shame" and "in the islands" (continued in v. 39 with "apparitions" and "daughters of sirens"), diverging sharply from the Hebrew.
notes.27:44: "Gaithan" (Γαιθάν) is a Septuagint-distinct place name where the Hebrew reads "an enduring pasture."
notes.28:1: Jeremiah 28 in the Septuagint corresponds to Jeremiah 51 in the Hebrew Bible.
notes.28:5: The Greek plural ton hagion ("the holy things" or "the holy ones") differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's singular "the Holy One of Israel" (Jer 51:5 MT).
notes.28:16: The Greek opening clause ("At a voice He set a roar of water") reflects a literal rendering of the Hebrew thunder idiom, and the closing clause reads phos ("light") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text (Jer 51:16) has "wind."
notes.28:20: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text (Jer 51:20) reads "You are My war-club," the Greek uses the verb diaskorpizeis ("You scatter") and repeats en soi ("in you," which can also be read instrumentally as "by you"), aligning with "from you" (v. 20) and "your commanders" (v. 23).
notes.28:27: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text (Jer 51:27) lists the kingdoms of "Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz," the Septuagint reads the first two as the command and phrase "raise ... from Me" (arate par' emou) and renders the third as the plural gentilic tois Aschanazeois ("to the Ashkenazites").
notes.28:34: The Greek reads "a thin darkness overtook me" (katelaben me skotos lepton) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text (Jer 51:34) reads "he has made me an empty vessel."
notes.28:49: Verses 45-48 of the Hebrew Masoretic Text (Jer 51:45-48) are absent from the Septuagint, so verse 49 continues the sentence directly from verse 44.
notes.28:58: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text (Jer 51:58), the Septuagint includes the negative ou ("will not labor in vain") and reads en arche ("in the beginning" or "in rule") where the Hebrew has "for fire."
notes.28:64: The Greek reads ton Chaldaion ("the Chaldeans") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text (Jer 51:64) reads "the disaster/evil," and omits the Masoretic closing line "Thus far are the words of Jeremiah."
notes.29:1: Jeremiah 29 in the Septuagint corresponds to Jeremiah 47 in the Hebrew Bible. Greek allophyloi ("foreigners") is the Septuagint's standard designation for the Philistines. In 29:4, the Greek speaks directly of wiping out Tyre and Sidon and "those who remain of the islands" (without Hebrew "Caphtor").
notes.29:5: The Greek reads Enakeim ("Anakim") where the Hebrew text has "their valley," and aperiphē ("has been cast away") where the Hebrew has "is silenced/destroyed."
notes.29:6: The Greek joins "How long will you slash" directly to the address to the sword of the Lord, and ends with eparthēti ("be lifted up" or "removed") where the Hebrew reads "be still."
notes.30:1: Chapter 30 in the Septuagint gathers four oracles against the nations (Idumea, Ammon, Kedar, and Damascus) in a different order from the Hebrew text (MT 49:1-33). Idumea is the standard Greek name for Edom; in 30:2, Greek "their place has been deceived" and "he has done grievous things" diverge markedly from the Hebrew.
notes.30:4: The Greek reads "by the hand of his brother, My neighbor" and links the end of 30:4 syntactically to the infinitive in 30:5 ("it is not possible to leave your orphan behind"), followed by "I will live" where the Hebrew reads "I will keep them alive."
notes.30:13: Greek Aitham ("Etham") renders the Hebrew adjective "perennial/enduring" as a proper place name, and "set the young men over her" reflects a different reading from the Hebrew. Similarly, in 30:15-16, the Greek reads "a cry of the sea was not heard" and "he will look" (for Hebrew "swoop") over "her strongholds" (for Hebrew "Bozrah").
